decision.meaning: Durable extinctions were strongly ordered toward smaller breeding groups within the same island-year risk sets, and one-year zero attrition greatly exceeded a simple proportional-thinning allocation null.

ecological_interpretation: The Palmer Adélie decline is not only a reduction in island totals or effective colony number. Loss is strongly ordered within islands: durable colony-code extinctions arise from groups that were much smaller immediately beforehand. The excess of zero transitions over a simple proportional-thinning null shows that this pattern is not reproduced by merely reallocating the observed declining abundance in proportion to current colony shares. This is consistent with size-dependent vulnerability, but the census data do not identify its biological cause.
supported_exploratory_statements: Within informative COR/HUM/LIT island-year risk sets, durable-extinction groups had a median of 5.5 breeding pairs immediately beforehand versus 47 pairs among same-stratum survivors.
The matched size coefficient was strongly negative and the within-stratum randomization statistic was extreme under the frozen exploratory calculation.
Observed one-year zero attrition on the stable-roster islands was 20 transitions versus a simple proportional-thinning null mean of 2.36 and 97.5% quantile of 5.
The same qualitative pattern was retained in the five-island sensitivity analysis.
not_supported: causal identification of social facilitation or an Allee effect
causal identification of snow or terrain
equating colony_code with a mapped physical subcolony polygon
calling this analysis preregistered or confirmatory
treating the proportional-thinning diagnostic as a complete demographic stochasticity model
next_gate: Use genuinely unopened endpoints to distinguish candidate mechanisms: first resolve chick-census duplicate-key semantics outcome-blind and freeze a chick-production test; independently freeze a species-by-terrain life-history test before outcome linkage.
